name: Iraq
genZNote: Iraq sits on ancient Mesopotamia, 'the land between two rivers' — the Tigris and Euphrates — where writing, cities, and law codes were invented millennia ago, which makes it one of the true starting points of recorded human civilization.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in West Asia, historically known as Mesopotamia ('land between the rivers'), centred on the Tigris and Euphrates river system.
Borders Iran, Turkey, Syria, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait, with a very short coastline on the Persian Gulf.
Terrain ranges from fertile river plains in the centre and south to mountains in the north (Kurdistan region) and desert in the west.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Arabic and Kurdish are both official languages, reflecting Iraq's major Arab and Kurdish population groups, alongside smaller minorities.
Home to some of the world's oldest civilizations — Sumer, Akkad, Babylon, and Assyria all flourished in ancient Mesopotamia.
Predominantly Muslim, split between Shia and Sunni communities, a divide that has significantly shaped modern Iraqi politics.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal parliamentary republic, with a President as head of state and a Prime Minister as head of government, established after the fall of Saddam Hussein's regime in 2003.
The Kurdistan Region in the north has significant autonomous self-governance within the federal Iraqi state.
Has experienced significant instability and conflict in recent decades, including the 2003 US-led invasion, sectarian conflict, and the fight against ISIS (2014-2017).

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding member of OPEC, with oil forming the overwhelming majority of government revenue.
Balances relationships between the United States, Iran (which holds significant political influence in Iraq), and neighbouring Arab states.
Member of the Arab League and United Nations, working to rebuild international standing after decades of conflict and sanctions.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: Iraq is one of India's top crude oil suppliers, making energy trade the cornerstone of the bilateral relationship.
India evacuated thousands of its citizens from Iraq during periods of conflict (e.g., 'Operation Raahat'-type responses), reflecting a historically significant Indian expatriate presence.
Ancient trade and cultural links between Mesopotamia and the Indian subcontinent date back millennia through Indus Valley-Mesopotamian trade contacts.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: An oil-dependent economy, with petroleum exports accounting for the vast majority of government revenue and GDP.
Reconstruction and infrastructure development remain major economic priorities following decades of conflict.
Agriculture along the Tigris-Euphrates river system remains historically and economically significant despite reduced water flows in recent decades.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the historical heart of ancient Mesopotamia, birthplace of writing, the wheel, and some of the earliest cities and law codes (e.g., the Code of Hammurabi).
Major global crude oil reserves and OPEC membership.
Significant 21st-century conflicts, including the 2003 invasion and the fight against ISIS.
The historically and archaeologically significant ancient city of Babylon.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Iraqi Dinar (IQD).
Economy heavily dependent on oil exports, which fund the majority of government revenue.
Recovering agricultural sector historically centred on the fertile land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Part of the historic Mesopotamian floodplain between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.
The Mesopotamian Marshes in the south, partially restored after being drained in the 1990s, are a UNESCO World Heritage wetland ecosystem.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Part of ancient Mesopotamia, often called the 'Cradle of Civilization', home to the Sumerians, Babylonians, and Assyrians.
Became an independent kingdom in 1932 after British mandate rule; became a republic in 1958.
Endured wars including the Iran-Iraq War (1980s), the 1991 Gulf War, and the 2003 US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1958 revolution ended the monarchy and established a republic.
The 2005 Constitution, adopted after the 2003 invasion, established a federal parliamentary democracy.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is the most popular sport; the national team won the AFC Asian Cup in 2007.
Home to ancient Babylon and Ur, among the world's most significant archaeological sites.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of the Arab League and OPEC.
Member of the UN and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Iraq is a West Asian federal parliamentary republic built on the historic land of Mesopotamia, a major OPEC oil producer working to rebuild after decades of conflict.
keyFacts: Federal parliamentary republic since 2003; Kurdistan Region has autonomous status.
Historic heart of ancient Mesopotamia (Sumer, Babylon, Assyria).
Founding OPEC member; major oil exporter.
commonConfusion: Iraq's modern political system (federal parliamentary republic) dates only from 2003, after the fall of Saddam Hussein — not to be confused with its much older ancient Mesopotamian civilizations.

highYieldFacts: Iraq: federal parliamentary republic since 2003; historic Mesopotamia; capital Baghdad.
Founding OPEC member; oil dominates government revenue.
India-Iraq: one of India's top crude oil suppliers.
commonTraps: Confusing ancient Mesopotamian history with Iraq's modern 2003-era political system.
Assuming Iraq is ethnically/linguistically homogeneous — Arabic and Kurdish are both official languages.
mustRemember: Iraq: Mesopotamian heartland, federal republic since 2003, OPEC founder, major India oil supplier.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-Iraq Relations
